features.description: Complete supported unnan subjunctive system; present second-person unne/unnen used as addressed commands.
features.scope_note: Cook §129 labels unne Imper.; Fulk §123 describes subjunctive substitution. Preserve both source descriptions, select the latter analysis for cell identity.

features.description: Both singular and plural commands of wyrcean.

Bounded adnominal genitive: possession/kinship, origin or belonging, and the agent or object relation to a verbal noun; the dependent genitive retains its own case inside an externally governed head phrase.
features.scope_note: Cook §153d incorrectly names ęgesan rather than Frēan as objective genitive; preserve the printed text and correct the analysis.

features.description: Recognize source setle his mægenðrymnesse: genitive of quality, naturally throne of his glory.
features.scope_note: Source-bound quality construction, not independent free productive abstract-genitive composition.

features.description: Substantival ān, sum and hwilc may select a genitive count group; the group stays genitive while the head has the case required by its clause.
features.scope_note: Contrast attributive ān agreeing with a singular noun. No unbounded quantity syntax.

features.description: Invariant fela takes genitive plural for the selected many/count-group frame.
features.scope_note: Do not infer micel +mass or general noun-of-measure syntax.

features.description: Choose case by the checked lexical frame: helpan+dative, geswīcan/gīeman+genitive, and new unnan/forwiernan+dative person+genitive thing.
features.scope_note: English object position does not decide Old English case; each lexical frame has separate evidence.

features.description: Unnan grants a genitive thing to a dative person.
Forwiernan refuses a genitive thing to a dative person.
Distinguish recipient, lexically governed person, beneficiary and experiencer. A shared dative form does not make the roles identical.
features.scope_note: Only separately documented lexical and prepositional frames are productive.

features.description: Use mid+dative for concrete means and distinguish it from accompaniment.
features.scope_note: Prose-default selected pattern; no Anglian mid+distinct instrument production.

features.description: Use the bounded bare instrumental means phrase in feeding: masculine/neuter singular strong-adjective -e and se ðȳ/ðon are distinct; nouns use the dative-shaped case form.
features.scope_note: Bare instrumental more characteristic of poetry than ordinary prose; teach as a supported stylistic choice, with mid+dative ordinary alternative. Other semantic instrument categories remain unassigned.

features.description: Produce selected se and strong gōd masculine/neuter singular instrumental cells. Feminine and plural have dative-shaped forms; nouns do not gain an invented ending.
features.scope_note: Retain mete-dat-sg identity and earlier analysis, adding contextual instrumental role. Other previously recognized pronoun instrumental forms are not silently promoted.

features.description: Subjectless hunger: accusative experiencer, third-singular hyngreð/hyngrede regardless of experiencer person/number.
features.scope_note: Selected two-cell finite system; genuine personal and alternative-case uses in the lexicon are outside this frame.

features.description: Ðyncð/ðūhte with dative experiencer and singular neuter nominative stimulus plus gōd; identify the expressed subject.
features.scope_note: Contrast true subjectless hunger. No new ðæt-content/infinitival/whole-passive judgment construction.

features.description: Present indicative can refer to future events where context supplies futurity; English will/shall need not produce willan.
features.scope_note: Willan remains volitional where intention is meant; no new periphrastic future tense.

features.description: Tō+dative gives a destination with come/go/fly.
features.scope_note: Separate from tō purpose/function and tō+inflected infinitive.

features.description: Bounded on ... hand uses accusative in the right/left-hand expression, including attested static standan.
features.scope_note: Bare hand supports accusative; weak swīðran alone is case-ambiguous. Ordinary on+dative location remains available; Cook warns rest/motion distinction is not invariant.

features.description: Bounded on+genitive possessor+naman expresses in someone’s name; naman is dative and the internal possessor genitive.
Beforan+dative person expresses standing before/in front of someone.
features.scope_note: Explicit promotion of prior source-only exposure.

features.description: Gesēon takes an accusative object with an agreeing accusative adjective describing its perceived condition.
features.scope_note: E.g. hungry/sick; do not convert it into the distinct accusative+infinitive frame.

features.description: Hīeran can take an accusative perceived actor with a plain infinitive naming its action.
features.scope_note: Explicit lexical extension distinct from prior gesēon frame; no general control/complement syntax.

features.description: The selected weak adjectives with the article can name people: the hungry, naked, sick, unrighteous; case and number follow their clause role.
features.scope_note: Plural people and an adjective modifying an expressed singular person must be distinguished. Do not imply every abstract substantive use is covered.

features.description: Fēdan takes accusative being fed; food may be expressed as mid+dative means or bounded bare instrumental means.
features.scope_note: Bare food example is new composition derived from independently checked lexical and case rules, not an exact quotation.

features.description: Scrȳdan clothes an accusative person.
features.scope_note: Garment mid+dative is documented reference evidence only; it is not an additional independently assigned lexical complement.

features.description: Andswarian answers a dative addressee, with a following direct quotation if expressed.
Scęncan pours accusative drink for a dative recipient.
Genēosian visits an accusative person in the selected frame.
features.scope_note: BT421 hine examples disambiguate accusative; nēosian genitive government is not denied.

features.description: Gewītan means depart/go away and may take fram+dative source.
features.scope_note: Not the distinct short-vowel preterite-present know.

features.description: Tōgelǣdan brings an accusative thing to a dative recipient.
features.scope_note: Promotes the actually supplied prior frame with full selected indicative morphology.

features.description: Dōn takes an accusative deed/it and dative affected person in the selected do-good-deeds-to frame.
Tōtwǣman separates an accusative being/group from a fram+dative other group.
features.scope_note: Explicit lexical extension of prior division frame; no new verbal paradigm.

features.description: Hwonne introduces a direct when-question using ordinary finite interrogative syntax.
features.scope_note: No temporal subordinate when-clause system is introduced.

features.description: Supplied sęllan +dative person +plain drincan: give someone to drink.
features.scope_note: Local Cook III.14.11 support; not independent recall of a general purpose construction.

features.description: Supplied swā lange swā ... expresses as long as / inasmuch as with the stated past actions.
features.scope_note: Supply both correlation tokens and lange. Cook p135 note17 explicitly observes inasmuch-as force; do not impose duration. No productive temporal-subordination system.

features.description: In bounded coordination with two different expressed subjects, recover the omitted repeated predicate from the preceding clause.
features.scope_note: Cook III.15.9 morning/night coming; source p134 the angels share the preceding coming predicate. No free deletion rule.

features.description: Wyrcean takes accusative work/deed, including cognate weorc, in the selected work/perform sense.
features.scope_note: Distinguish this new ordinary sense from the earlier yield-fruit frame.

features.description: Promote the separately registered cīepan/bycgan plain infinitives for deliberate willan and blāwan for the new hīeran-perception construction.
features.scope_note: Only plain-infinitive use in these defined frames. Earlier supplied citation status is preserved historically.

paradigms.title: unnan: SUBJ
paradigms.scope: All persons, singular/plural, present/preterite; unne/unnen serve as singular/plural addressed command substitutes. No formal unnað paradigm is invented.

paradigms.title: hyngran: IMPERSONAL-IND
paradigms.scope: The complete selected third-singular present/preterite impersonal indicative system, with accusative experiencer and no nominative subject. Personal uses and alternative experiencer case exist but are outside this assigned frame.

paradigms.title: ðyncan: EXPERIENCER-IND
paradigms.scope: The complete selected third-singular present/preterite indicative system with dative experiencer and a singular neuter nominative stimulus (hit/ðæt/ðis) plus gōd. This expressed-subject construction is not the subjectless hunger frame.
